items.text: Studied from age 7 under the master Pyoam Kang Sehwang in Ansan

items.venue: Entered royal service as a court painter (hwawon) of the Dohwaseo, on Kang Sehwang's recommendation

items.title: Portrait of the Royal Heir (the future King Jeongjo)
Royal Portrait of King Yeongjo (assisting Byeon Sang-byeok)
Institutional paintings commissioned by King Jeongjo, including Kyujanggak and the main hall of Yongjusa
Feast for the Pyongyang Governor (평양감사 향안도)
Danwon pungsokdo cheop, album of 25 genre paintings of everyday life
Chuseongbu (Landscape in an autumn night) and Samgongbulhwando (after 1800)

items.text: National Museum of Korea, Seoul (Danwon pungsokdo cheop, designated National Treasure/Treasure No. 527)
Art names Danwon (Tanwŏn) and others; one of the 'Three Wons' with Hyewon and Owon
Died in poverty; year of death uncertain (1806, 1810 or after 1814 depending on source)
Ansan's Danwon-gu district and annual Danwon Art Festival are named after him
Pratt, Rutt and Hoare, Korea: A Historical and Cultural Dictionary, Routledge
Jane Turner (ed.), Grove Dictionary of Art, Oxford University Press
Oh Joosok, 'The Life and Art of Kim Hong-do', Korean Art and Archaeology vol. 1, National Museum of Korea
